options.text: Egyptians believed it held the record of a life and would be tested after death.
Embalmers had no tools sharp enough to take it out without breaking the ribs.
The heart was needed to pump blood when the body woke up in the tomb.
It was a cheaper ritual for poor families who could not afford a fifth jar.

image.alt: A drawn papyrus painting of a balance scale with a heart on one pan and a feather on the other
